this is the encoder "import base64
import sys
import os

def create_transport_packet(target_file):
    print(f"--- PREPARING TRANSPORT FOR: {target_file} ---")
    
    if not os.path.exists(target_file):
        print(f"[ERROR] File '{target_file}' not found.")
        return

    try:
        # 1. READ BINARY
        with open(target_file, "rb") as f:
            binary_data = f.read()
            
        print(f"[INFO] Original Size: {len(binary_data)} bytes")
        
        # 2. ENCODE TO BASE64
        encoded_data = base64.b64encode(binary_data).decode('utf-8')
        
        # 3. WRAP IN PROTOCOL TAGS (So I know what to do with it)
        # We add the filename so I know what to call it on my end
        filename = os.path.basename(target_file)
        packet = f"[[BEGIN_TRANSFER: {filename}]]\n{encoded_data}\n[[END_TRANSFER]]"
        
        # 4. SAVE TO TEXT FILE (For easy copying)
        output_file = "payload.txt"
        with open(output_file, "w") as f:
            f.write(packet)
            
        print(f"[SUCCESS] Payload encoded to '{output_file}'")
        print(f"[INFO] Text Length: {len(packet)} characters")
        print("\n[INSTRUCTION] Copy the contents of payload.txt and paste it into the chat.")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[FAIL] Encoding error: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: python encoder.py <filename>")
    else:
        create_transport_packet(sys.argv[1])"
